title: Life's smallest rooms
question: What are living things made of, and how do cells differ?
hook: Every living thing, from bacteria to animals, is built from cells, and cells come in two basic designs.
idea: All cells share a membrane around cytoplasm with genetic material, but prokaryotes lack a nucleus while eukaryotes have one.

beats.prompt: Under a microscope you see a single-celled organism whose DNA floats in the cytoplasm with no nuclear membrane around it. What is it most likely to be?

choices.label: A yeast
choices.feedback: Yeasts are single-celled, which tempts, but they are eukaryotes and so have a nucleus.

choices.label: A somatic cell from an animal
choices.feedback: Animal body cells are eukaryotic, so their nucleus is enclosed in a membrane.

choices.label: A cell from a plant
choices.feedback: Plants are eukaryotes, so their cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.

beats.explain: Prokaryotes, which include bacteria and archaea, are single-celled and have a nucleoid instead of a membrane-bound nucleus.

beats.prompt: Match each name to its place in the story of the cell.
beats.explain: Hooke discovered cells, Schleiden and Schwann developed cell theory, and Thiomargarita magnifica is the largest bacterium known.

beats.prompt: Sort each organism into its cell type.
beats.explain: Bacteria and archaea are prokaryotes; yeasts, animals and plants are eukaryotes.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning about yeasts is wrong. Which?
steps: So a yeast would have a nucleoid, not a nucleus.
beats.explain: Eukaryotes can be single-celled too; yeasts are single-celled eukaryotes, so being one cell does not make an organism a prokaryote.
